# gannet

> gannet is an open-source deep research agent being built in C# on Microsoft Agent Framework by DBHQ. Give it a question and it plans the research, searches the web, weighs each source and writes a report in which every claim is cited to a page the run actually fetched. It is in development and not released yet.

Status: in development. The core is merged (citation checking and numbering in APA, MLA, Chicago and IEEE; credibility scoring; report export; run storage). The model and search providers, the research workflow, the command line, REST API, MCP server and web UI are still being built.

Source: https://github.com/dbhq-uk/gannet (MIT licence). A rewrite of https://github.com/tarun7r/deep-research-agent by Tarun Sai Goddu (MIT).

## Pages

- [gannet](https://gannet.dbhq.uk/): what gannet is being built to do, the rules it keeps about citations and stored text, and where the build stands.
- [Open-source deep research](https://gannet.dbhq.uk/open-source-deep-research/): the open-source deep research agents compared - licence, search backends, local models and how each cites its sources.
- [Perplexity alternatives](https://gannet.dbhq.uk/perplexity-alternative/): hosted and self-hosted alternatives to Perplexity, and how to test whether one is a real replacement.
- [Source credibility](https://gannet.dbhq.uk/source-credibility/): what source credibility is, the theory behind it, and the CRAAP, SIFT and lateral reading methods for judging a source.
- [SearXNG search API](https://gannet.dbhq.uk/searxng-search-api/): run SearXNG in Docker, enable its JSON API, call it from code and use it as a free search API for an agent.

## The rules gannet keeps

1. Every citation points at a page the run fetched. Sources get IDs when they are fetched; the writer cites only those IDs; anything else is removed.
2. No search or reader result text is written to disk. Page text lives in memory for one run.
3. You choose the model (cloud, or local through Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp) and the search service, per run.
